title: Egypt Entrance Tickets: What Tours Include and What Costs Extra
excerpt: Egypt entrance fees: which tickets your tour already includes, which tombs and pyramid interiors cost extra, and November 2026 prices, with Giza tours from €29.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Yes: the entrance tickets for the sites named on a tour's itinerary are normally part of the tour price. The extras are separate tickets: the Great Pyramid interior (EGP 1,500, about €25), Tutankhamun's tomb (KV62, EGP 700, about €12), Seti I's tomb (KV17, EGP 2,000, about €33) and the tomb of Ramesses V and VI (KV9, EGP 220, about €4). Nefertari's tomb (QV66) has been closed since March 2024. Read the tour's included and not-included lists, price the extras you want on the official ticket portal, and budget for them before you go. Prices are as of November 2026, converted at EGP 60 to the euro (8 November 2026).

Use the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities monument pages to check site information and visiting details before you travel.

Key facts

Fact Detail

Join it on Sawa Giza Uncovered, about 4 hours, from €29 per person · Luxor in Depth, full day, from €75 per person (both as listed in November 2026)

The tour price looks settled, and then the ticket window, or the tour's fine print, mentions a second set of prices. Egypt's sites run a two-tier ticket system, and it catches almost every first-time visitor: one ticket covers the site, while a handful of special tombs and pyramid interiors need their own tickets. This post maps the whole system: what your tour already covers, what costs extra, what the reported prices are, and how to check them before you book. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace, shows the included and not-included lists on its tour pages, and our team has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

Are Egypt entrance fees included in tour prices?

Yes: the entrance fees for the sites named on a tour's itinerary are part of the tour price on most tours, and the inclusions list says so. On Sawa's page for Luxor in Depth, the full-day East and West Bank tour, "Entrance tickets" appear in the included list, while "Special tombs (Tutankhamun, Nefertari)" and "Gratuities" appear under not included (checked 8 November 2026). On Giza Uncovered, the included list names the entrance ticket to the Giza Plateau, the panorama viewpoint and the Great Sphinx, and the not-included list names entrance inside the Great Pyramid of Khufu or other pyramids. The trap is booking without reading the lists: the lowest-priced listings elsewhere sometimes leave tickets out entirely and surprise you at the gate.

What costs extra: pyramid interiors and special tombs

Two families of tickets are rarely included in an Egypt tour price: pyramid interiors and the flagship royal tombs. You buy them as separate tickets, online or at the site, on top of the general entry ticket, not instead of it. The table lists foreign-adult prices as of November 2026; treat every figure as a budget guide and confirm it on the official portal before you travel.

Site Extra ticket Adult price (November 2026) In the general ticket?
Giza Plateau Great Pyramid (Khufu) interior EGP 1,500 (about €25) No: separate ticket
Giza Plateau Khafre interior about EGP 280 (about €4.70) No: separate ticket
Giza Plateau Menkaure interior reported between EGP 200 and EGP 280; open only at times No: separate ticket
Valley of the Kings, Luxor Tutankhamun's tomb (KV62) EGP 700 (about €12) No: the general ticket covers three other tombs
Valley of the Kings, Luxor Seti I's tomb (KV17) EGP 2,000 (about €33) No
Valley of the Kings, Luxor Ramesses V and VI tomb (KV9) EGP 220 (about €4) No
Valley of the Queens, Luxor Nefertari's tomb (QV66) last reported price EGP 2,000 (about €33) No. Closed since March 2024, with no reopening date announced

The Great Pyramid figure is the one to check hardest. It rose to EGP 1,500 from 1 January 2025, as Egypt Independent reported, although the Ministry's own page still shows EGP 1,000 and some guides quote older figures. Students pay half price at Giza.

The Grand Egyptian Museum is the other ticket that moved recently: EGP 1,830 for a foreign adult (EGP 920 for students and children) from 1 November 2026, sold online only at tickets.gem.eg. Sawa's Giza Pyramids, Sphinx and GEM tour, 8 hours from €71 per person as listed in November 2026, includes both the plateau and museum tickets and lunch; see the pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day. Prices also move: the Ministry has revised fees several times in recent years, so a figure copied from a 2023 blog post is already history. Budget on today's reported numbers, then re-check a week before you fly.

The Valley of the Kings rule: three tombs, then extra tickets

One Valley of the Kings ticket (EGP 750) covers three open standard tombs, chosen at the ticket window from the list that is open that day; everything beyond that is an extra ticket. Your guide can advise which three have the best condition-to-crowd balance on the day. Tutankhamun (KV62), Seti I (KV17) and Ramesses V and VI (KV9) are not part of the three: each needs its own ticket. Nefertari's tomb (QV66) sits in a separate necropolis, the Valley of the Queens, and has its own ticket too, but it has been closed since March 2024, so do not build a day around it. Tombs also rotate closed, so confirm which are open the week you travel. The Grand West Bank tour, from €60 per person as listed in November 2026, pairs the valley with Deir el-Medina, the workers' village; like every Sawa tour, it never includes the special tombs.

Luxor Pass and Cairo Pass: when a pass beats single tickets

For most visitors it does not. The Luxor Pass (Standard US$130 or €120) costs more than the four main Luxor sites plus Tutankhamun's tomb bought one by one: the Valley of the Kings (EGP 750), Karnak (EGP 600), Luxor Temple (EGP 500) and the Temple of Hatshepsut (EGP 440) come to EGP 2,290 (about €38), or EGP 2,990 (about €50) with KV62, at the October 2026 prices reported by Explore Luxor. A pass only starts to pay off if you plan to visit most of the sites on the fee list within its five days.

The Premium tier adds Seti I and Nefertari. With Nefertari closed, Premium buys you Seti I (EGP 2,000, about €33) for a pass price of US$250 (€220), so it is hard to justify. The Cairo Pass is reported at US$130 (€120); on 2025 prices, a Cairo day of Giza (EGP 700), Saqqara (EGP 600), Dahshur (EGP 300) and the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir (EGP 550) comes to about EGP 2,150 (about €36). Neither pass covers the Great Pyramid interior. Passes are sold in person, not online, against your passport details and a passport photo.

Pass Price (Ministry tariff, January 2024; Cairo Pass from a 2026 secondary report) Covers Worth it when
Luxor Pass, Standard US$130 or €120 · students US$70 or €60 Luxor sites for 5 days; excludes the Nefertari and Seti I tombs You will visit most of the sites on the Luxor fee list in five days
Luxor Pass, Premium US$250 or €220 · students US$130 or €120 As Standard, plus the Nefertari and Seti I tombs Only if Nefertari reopens and you plan to enter both premium tombs
Cairo Pass US$130 or €120 · students about half Archaeological sites and museums in Greater Cairo for 5 days (the Ministry tariff excludes the National Museum of Egyptian Civilisation) You plan several full days of Cairo sites and museums

How to check today's Egypt entrance fees before you book

Check prices on egymonuments.com, the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities' online booking site; buying there also keeps you away from resellers. Three practical habits. Price your extras on the portal before booking a tour. Buy the Great Pyramid interior ticket early in your visit, at the Pyramids Visitor Centre, the plateau's main entrance on the Cairo to Fayoum road, or online. And carry a card as well as cash. Guides report that Giza tickets are now card only; at the Valley of the Kings, tickets are sold at the Visitor Centre and a card is effectively required, and the Tombs of the Nobles are cashless in the 2026 season.

What tours include on Sawa departures

Sawa lists the inclusions on each tour page, so the ticket maths happens before you book. Two examples, with prices per person as listed in November 2026 and fixed per traveller. Giza Uncovered, the pyramids tour of about four hours, is from €29 and lists the Giza Plateau entrance ticket as included; camel rides and entrance inside the Great Pyramid are on the not-included list. Luxor in Depth, from €75, lists entrance tickets as included and special tombs (Tutankhamun and Nefertari) as not included. One worked Luxor budget: €75 for the tour, plus Tutankhamun's tomb at EGP 700 (about €12), comes to about €87 per person before tips, drinks and food (check the departure page for lunch). Nefertari's tomb is not part of any budget at present, because it is closed.

How to do it with Sawa Tours

Every Sawa departure is a shared date on a fixed catalogue tour: one tour, one day, four to eight travellers, and a new independent departure when a date fills. Seats are sold by licensed agencies, and one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date operates it, named before the deposit is due. Reserving a seat is free, with no card, and nothing is charged before the date confirms. The date confirms (the GoAhead) when four travellers have reserved it, and then you pay a 10% deposit by a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. The balance is due 2 days (48 hours) before departure. A date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Cancelling at least 48 hours before departure is a full refund; under 48 hours you lose the 10% deposit; force majeure means a full refund. Sawa Tours is operated by Online Era (registration 148500). The full rules are in how the GoAhead works, on how Sawa works and in the terms. Compare ticket-inclusive tours on Sawa's itineraries, or browse forming departures for dates already close to confirming.

The verdict on Egypt entrance fees

Read every Egypt tour price as general entry plus extras: the standard sites on the itinerary are included, while pyramid interiors and the premium tombs (KV62, KV17, and QV66 if it reopens) are separate tickets you price on the official portal. Skip the passes unless you plan a heavy five days of sites. Pick your extras, add them to the tour price, then book: compare ticket-inclusive itineraries on Sawa and reserve a seat free.

faq.q: Are entrance fees included in Egypt tours?
faq.a: Usually yes for standard site entry: tours generally include the general ticket for every site on the itinerary, and the inclusions list says so. What is rarely included are the special tickets: pyramid interiors, Tutankhamun's tomb (KV62), Seti I (KV17) and, if it reopens, Nefertari (QV66). Read the included and not-included lists before paying, and budget the extras separately.

faq.q: Which Valley of the Kings tombs cost extra?
faq.a: Three tombs sit outside the general three-tomb ticket: Tutankhamun (KV62) at EGP 700 (about €12), Seti I (KV17), the valley's grandest, at EGP 2,000 (about €33), and Ramesses V and VI (KV9) at EGP 220 (about €4). Nefertari's tomb (QV66) is in the Valley of the Queens; its last reported price was EGP 2,000, and it has been closed since March 2024. All figures are as of November 2026.

faq.q: Is the Great Pyramid interior ticket worth it?
faq.a: For many first-time visitors, yes. It costs EGP 1,500 (about €25) on top of the EGP 700 plateau ticket, and climbing the Grand Gallery to the King's Chamber is a once-only experience. The honest downsides: the passages are steep, narrow and hot, with a low stooped section. Skip it if claustrophobia or knee trouble is a concern.

faq.q: Do the Luxor Pass and Cairo Pass include the special tombs?
faq.a: Partly. The Ministry tariff says the Luxor Pass Premium adds the Nefertari and Seti I tombs, while the Standard pass excludes them. It does not say that Tutankhamun's tomb (KV62) is included, so assume it is not and check at the ticket office. The Cairo Pass covers Cairo-area sites but, according to 2026 reports, not the Great Pyramid interior. For most visitors, single tickets cost less than either pass.

faq.q: Can I buy Egypt site tickets online in advance?
faq.a: Yes: the Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities sells tickets through its booking site, egymonuments.com, where you choose a site and date and pay by card. It is the surest way to price your extras before you go. The Grand Egyptian Museum sells its own tickets online only, at tickets.gem.eg. Passes are the exception: they are sold in person only.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure never fills?
faq.a: Nothing is charged before a date reaches four travellers and gets its GoAhead. A date has until 7 days before the tour to reach four; if it does not, it is cancelled, you pay nothing, and Sawa suggests another date. Once a date is confirmed, it is not cancelled for low numbers, and the tour keeps running for the others if someone drops out or does not pay.
